subject: Request to remove single conversation from logs (RQ-DEL011)
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@acmecloud.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data deletion request — single conversation (internal thread id 99-ACME-DEL)

Hi Ben,

We need Redwood's help removing a single customer conversation from all analytics and operational logs. The conversation is internal thread id 99-ACME-DEL (we also have a local reference RQ-DEL011). This is a data residency/retention exception: the user invoked a right-to-be-forgotten request under their local residency policy and Acme must ensure that the conversation does not remain in downstream logs used for debugging/analytics.

Can you confirm the scope of what you will remove (in-memory caches, request logs, replay data, and any derived analytics), and whether this will also remove references in aggregated metrics? We also need an ETA — this is a compliance ask with a hard deadline on Dec 3.

I've attached the minimal log slice and the user's retention exception form.

Attachment: [log_slice_RQ-DEL011.csv (CSV, 12KB)]
Attachment: [retention_exception_RQ-DEL011.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morris
Privacy & Compliance, Acme Cloud
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@acmecloud.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion request — single conversation (internal thread id 99-ACME-DEL)

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and attachments. We can take action on RQ-DEL011 but need to be precise about scope and downstream systems. High-level plan: 

- Ops will remove the conversation from request logs and the serving KV caches where the conversation is present.
- We will flag and remove the conversation from analytics pipelines where feasible; aggregated metrics that are irreversible (pre-aggregated rollups older than our aggregation window) cannot be "uncomputed" but we'll note the deletion for audit and exclude affected rows from future reports.
- Backups and immutable snapshots: we'll need to log an exception and a remediation note; we cannot retroactively delete from backups without additional legal review.

Can you confirm you only want removal from operational logs, analytics, and caches (not backups), and that the Acme compliance team approves the backup exception? If yes, please reply confirming and we'll route to Ops for execution.

I’ve looped in Jasmine (CS lead) to coordinate the runbook and Grace (Privacy lead) to sign off on the exception language.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena@acmecloud.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion request — RQ-DEL011: proposed runbook

Thanks Elena — confirming scope = operational logs (request/trace logs), serving caches (KV/prefix caches), and analytics staging tables (pre-aggregation). Per Ben's note, we will NOT touch immutable backups until legal confirms; we'll mark those snapshots with an exception tag.

Proposed runbook (Ops):
1) Validate incoming log slice (attached) to locate canonical conversation keys.
2) Execute targeted deletion script against request logs (time-bounded) and remove KV cache entries.
3) Recompute affected analytic staging partitions where possible and mark aggregates impacted with an audit flag (metadata entry: RQ-DEL011).
4) Create Jira ticket OPS-7321 and attach exec logs, then notify Acme compliance.

ETA: 48 business hours after Acme confirms backup exception. Expected outage/impact: negligible (read-only during a 10m window for targeted deletions).

I'll attach the deletion script stub and Jira link to the Ops ticket when we kick it off.

Attachments: [deletion_runbook_stub.sh (sh, 4KB)]

-jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, jasmine.liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion request — RQ-DEL011: legal sign-off and next steps

Elena — thank you for confirming earlier by email that Acme accepts the backup exception and signs off on retaining immutable snapshots for audit. With that consent, Redwood authorizes Ops to proceed with the targeted deletion scope Jasmine outlined.

We will:
- Open OPS-7321 (linked above) and add a retention-exception record.
- Run the targeted deletions during the maintenance window tonight (11:45pm PT) and post execution logs to the Jira ticket.
- Provide a short forensic report (what was deleted, affected tables, and confirmation that KV caches were evicted).

Note on monitoring: because some analytics partitions will be recomputed, expect minor variance in cohort counts for the window 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-30; we will annotate downstream reports so Acme analysts are aware.

If you need an exec-signed attestation PDF for your records after completion, say the word and we will produce it.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
